neighbours.label: restriction to the nominal or minimal ('only on paper', 'mere', 'only temporary', 'if only in name'): something is less real or substantial than claimed
fire: The new regulations exist only on paper and are never enforced.
The president's role is largely ceremonial, a mere figurehead.
The discount offers only temporary relief from rising prices.
The union was a partnership in name only.
His apology was a mere formality that changed nothing.
The reforms were cosmetic, just window dressing for foreign donors.
The board met, if only to rubber-stamp the decisions already made.
The fine amounted to little more than a slap on the wrist.
quiet: The new regulations are strictly enforced by the inspectors.
The president holds real executive power over the army.
The discount brought lasting relief from rising prices.
The union was a close and active partnership for decades.
His apology led to a complete change in company policy.
The reforms transformed the courts and the tax system.
The board met and debated every decision at length.
The fine was large enough to bankrupt the company.

notes: Card: ' only' x4, ' on' x4, ' just' x3, ' mere', 'amounted to'; output promotes ' symbolic', ' paper', ' moral', ' symbol'. The - pole is ' political'/' domestic'/' internal' (substantive real-world causes), plausibly the other side: nominal vs actual. Near misses keep topic but state substance.
